title: Not sacrifice alone: Scripture condemns even the sacred kiss (Job 31)
source_text: LXXVII. Neque est quod dicat aliquis Ethnicos ab Apostolo accusari Latriae creaturis exhibitae, quoniam obtulerunt eis sacrificia, quae omnium confessione ad Latriae cultum spectant. Nam Scriptura sacra non solum Gentes damnat quod creaturis immolarint, sed vel eo nomine quod illas osculo sacro coluerint. A quo crimine vir Sanctus Job protestatur se fuisse immunem, Si vidi, inquit, solem quum fulgeret, & lunam incedentem clare: Et laetatum est, sive potius seductum est in abscondito cor meum, & osculatus sum manum meam ore meo. Job. 31. 26.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is there reason why someone should say that the Heathen are accused by the Apostle of Latria shown to creatures because they offered sacrifices to them, which by the confession of all belong to the worship of Latria. For sacred Scripture condemns the Gentiles not only because they sacrificed to creatures, but even on this account, that they worshipped them with a sacred kiss. From which crime the holy man Job protests that he was free: If I saw, he says, the sun when it shone, and the moon walking brightly; and my heart rejoiced, or rather was enticed, in secret, and I kissed my hand with my mouth. Job 31:26.
pass_b_english: Nor can anyone say that the reason the Apostle accuses the pagans of giving latria to creatures is that they offered them sacrifices, which everyone admits belong to the worship of latria. For Holy Scripture condemns the Gentiles not only for sacrificing to creatures, but even for worshiping them with a sacred kiss.

The holy man Job protests that he was innocent of this crime: "If I looked at the sun when it shone, and at the moon moving in brightness, and my heart rejoiced, or rather was secretly enticed, and I kissed my hand with my mouth" (Job 31:26-27).

choices.term: laetatum est, sive potius seductum est
choices.english: rejoiced, or rather was secretly enticed
choices.why: Le Blanc corrects the Vulgate 'laetatum' by the Hebrew sense 'enticed'; the English keeps his correction.
